newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan economy seen at zero growth in 1997 - centre.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan economy seen at zero growth in 1997 - centre.

text.p: Morocco's think tank Centre Marocain de Conjoncture (CMC) said on Thursday the economy may stagnate in 1997 mainly because of falling cereals output.
"On the basis of the climate of negative changes in recent months, the centre revised its previous optimistic growth forecast to a more modest expectation," it said.

"Therefore we expect a stagnation of Morocco's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in 1997 and probably a negative growth of minus one percent in the worst of cases, due mainly to an expected 50 percent drop in cereals harvest."
Agriculture composes nearly 20 percent of Morocco's GDP and employs 50 percent of its estimated 10 million workforce.
Morocco's GDP jumped to 11.8 percent in 1996 from minus 7.6 percent in 1995. It reached in value $34.7 billion the same year against $31.8 billion in 1995, the Statistics Directorate said.
Morocco harvested 10 million tonnes of cereals in 1995/96 against 1.6 million tonnes in 1994/95, when it was hit by what authorities described as the drought of the century.

The finance ministry had said GDP would grow between 3.5 and 4.0 percent this year based on modest cereals harvest of 7.0 million tonnes. But in the last three months most farming areas suffered from lack of rain and cereals were affected.
CMC said Morocco's non-agricultural production was expected to grow by 3.9 percent by the end of 1997.
